description: A fang as long as a hand, worn blunt at the tip. Tuskmaul has broken plenty on other people's shields.
lore: Buyers want them blunt, and the reasoning is not sentiment. A fang worn round at the point has been in service a long time, which means the animal carrying it is old and settled and accounted for, standing where it has stood since before anyone thought to look — the way [[monsters/gray_brute_2|the old bull]] stands. A sharp one has come off something that has not finished growing.

So the blunt fetches thirty-two gold and the sharp fetches half, and the difference has nothing to do with ivory. It is the arithmetic. Somewhere in country that everybody has agreed for two hundred years is empty, on ground people cross without looking up, there is a new one. The man who brings a sharp fang to a counter is asked where he found it, politely, immediately, and by everybody in the room at once.
gm_notes: Price as fieldcraft. A sharp fang is a live rumour hook: something young is on ground the trade considers settled.
